items.definition:
a person who looks after a church and churchyard, sometimes acting as a bell-ringer and grave-digger
The sexton was responsible for maintaining the church grounds.

a ghost or phantom; something widely feared as a possible unpleasant or dangerous occurrence
The specter of unemployment loomed over the town.

the branch of science concerned with classification, especially of organisms; a classification of things or concepts
The taxonomy of plants is a complex field of study.

a ruler exercising authority in a colony on behalf of a sovereign
The viceroy governed the vast colonial territory.

the sixth letter of the Greek alphabet
The symbol for the Riemann zeta function is ζ.

a person who practiced alchemy
The alchemist sought to turn lead into gold.

a story, poem, or picture that can be interpreted to reveal a hidden meaning
George Orwell's 'Animal Farm' is a political allegory.

illegal or unauthorized goods
He was caught selling bootleg copies of the movie.

the study and treatment of heart diseases
He decided to specialize in cardiology after medical school.

a complex carbohydrate found in plant cell walls
Wood is primarily composed of cellulose.

the components of an electric circuit
The complex circuitry of the computer allows it to perform many tasks.

a financial officer, especially in government or a large company
The comptroller is responsible for managing the organization's finances.

skill in performing tasks, especially with the hands
The surgeon showed great dexterity during the delicate operation.

the state of being exclusive
The contract granted the company exclusivity for distribution in the region.

an unpleasant or contemptible person, especially one who acts as an informer
Don't be a fink and tell on your friends.

humanist
He was a strong advocate for humanist values and education.

industrialization
The industrialization of the country led to rapid economic growth.

issuer
The bank is the issuer of the credit card.

lancet
The doctor used a lancet to prick the patient's finger.

belief in spiritual truth through direct experience
Her studies focused on ancient forms of mysticism.

a person who goes ahead and discovers or opens up a new path or way
The explorers were pathfinders in the uncharted territory.

a strong or habitual liking for something or tendency to do something
She has a penchant for spicy food.

The practice or custom of having more than one wife or husband at the same time.
Polygamy is illegal in many countries.

The minimum number of members of an assembly or society that must be present at any of its meetings to make the proceedings of that meeting valid.
The meeting could not start until a quorum was present.

A light theatrical entertainment consisting of a series of short sketches, songs, and dances, typically satirizing contemporary events and prominent people.
They went to see a musical revue in the city.

The quality of being extremely thorough, exhaustive, or accurate.
The scientific study was conducted with great rigor.

A person with a personality disorder manifesting itself in extreme antisocial attitudes and behavior and a lack of conscience.
The character in the movie was portrayed as a dangerous sociopath.

an annual calendar containing important dates and statistical information
The farmer consulted his almanac for the best planting dates.

a statue of gigantic size and proportions
The new skyscraper is a colossus dominating the city skyline.

the transfer or delegation of power to a lower level
The government proposed further devolution of powers to the regions.

an organic compound formed from an acid and an alcohol
Many fruits get their distinctive smells from esters.

a form of arthritis
He suffered from a painful attack of gout in his big toe.

an organic compound consisting entirely of hydrogen and carbon
Petroleum is a complex mixture of various hydrocarbons.

institute (often used in names of organizations)
She is a researcher at the Pasteur Institut in Paris.

a distinctive doctrine, theory, system, or practice
The debate often revolved around various political 'isms'.

sexual desire
Freud's theories often discuss the concept of libido.

a magician or sorcerer
The powerful mage cast a spell.

a name or nickname
He earned the moniker "Speedy" for his quick reflexes.

the central part of a church
The congregation gathered in the nave of the cathedral.

the state of having two opposite tendencies, opinions, or aspects
There was a clear polarity between their political views.

the return of someone to their own country
The government organized the repatriation of its citizens from the war zone.

a mass for the repose of the souls of the dead
Mozart's Requiem is a powerful and moving piece of music.

a swamp or marshy area; a piece of dead skin or tissue that has been shed.
The explorers had to navigate through a muddy slough.

a fixed or movable habitation, typically of light construction; a place of worship.
The ancient Israelites built a tabernacle as a portable sanctuary.

an object, typically an inscribed ring or stone, that is thought to have magic powers and to bring good luck.
He carried a small stone as a good luck talisman.

a female figure who chooses those who may die in battle and carries them to Valhalla
In Norse mythology, a Valkyrie guides fallen warriors to Valhalla.

intense or irrational dislike or fear of people from other countries
The rise of xenophobia is a concern in many societies.

a great enemy of Christ expected to appear before the end of the world
Some interpretations of prophecy speak of the coming of the Antichrist.

the rearing of aquatic animals or the cultivation of aquatic plants for food
Aquaculture is becoming an important source of seafood.

the action or process of making or becoming greater in size or amount
The company announced an augmentation of its workforce.

a collection of concise information
The book is a compendium of ancient myths.

an organization or effort for the preservation of something
The land conservancy worked to protect the local wetlands.

the most important or difficult part of a problem or issue
The crux of the argument was whether the evidence was admissible.

a point of transition or change
She was on the cusp of a major career breakthrough.

the process by which a beam of light or other system of waves is spread out as a result of passing through a narrow aperture or across an edge, typically accompanied by interference between the wave components
Light diffraction causes the rainbow patterns seen on a CD.

the Christian ceremony commemorating the Last Supper, in which bread and wine are consecrated and consumed
Catholics receive the Eucharist during Mass.

intense and passionate feeling
The crowd cheered with great fervor for their team.

a person believing in or practicing religious heresy
He was accused of being a heretic for questioning church doctrines.

a sharp projection; a sudden burst of activity
He went on a jag of spending after winning the lottery.

a false show or pretense; a costume ball
His kindness was just a masquerade for his true intentions.

a sensational dramatic piece with exaggerated characters and exciting events
The play was a classic melodrama, full of over-the-top emotions.

excessive self-admiration
His extreme narcissism made it difficult for him to empathize with others.

a model of excellence
He was considered a paragon of virtue by his peers.

a metal link or ring, used to fasten a prisoner
The prisoner was held in shackles.
